title: Evidence acceptance criteria and auditor scripts for RBACv2 + SIEM exports
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc defines the acceptance criteria for automated evidence for RBACv2 and audit-log exports into our SIEM, and provides a short set of auditor-facing scripts and Q&A talking points for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 engagements. It is intended to be used in dry runs (playtests) with external auditors and by our control owners to validate evidence pipelines before an audit window.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- What we want auditors to see: consistent, tamper-evident audit streams from authz/authn and admin planes; documented mapping from events to control objectives; an automated evidence bundle with sampling proof and verification steps.
- Key systems in scope: RBACv2 service (policy store + enforcement logs), identity provider (IdP) audit logs, orchestration for SIEM export (kafka -> transformation -> siem-ingest), and the evidence automation job (evidence-orch).
- Acceptance criteria are split into: schema-level checks, delivery guarantees, retention / immutable storage proof, sampling & traceability, and human-readable artefacts for auditors.

1) Evidence acceptance criteria (pass/fail checklist)
A. Schema and field-level checks (SIEM export)
  - Exported events must include a stable event_type and event_id (UUID v4) for dedup and correlation.
  - Required fields: timestamp_utc, event_id, event_type, actor_id, actor_email (if available), target_resource, action, outcome (success|failure), request_id (trace id), source_service, consented_ip, and k8s_pod_hash (if from cluster).
  - RBAC delta events must include: policy_version, change_author, change_diff_hash, and policy_prior_version_id.
  - Failure: any export missing >1 required field in a 1000-event sliding window -> fail.

B. Delivery and integrity guarantees
  - End-to-end latency: 95th percentile of events visible in SIEM <= 60s for authz/authn flows in production traffic tests.
  - At-least-once delivery with dedup on event_id; documented dedup window.
  - Tamper evidence: retained original signed blob (SHA256) stored in evidence-store (immutable bucket) alongside SIEM records. Evidence automation must surface the signature and hash in the auditor bundle.

C. Retention & access controls
  - Events required by SOC2/ISO must be retained for 1 year (default) with snapshot capabilities to 3 years for enterprise customers.
  - Access to evidence-store is limited to sec-compliance and designated SREs; access requests are logged and included in evidence bundle.

D. Sampling & traceability
  - Evidence automation must include a deterministic sample seed and algorithm used to select N events for deep inspection. Auditor bundle includes seed and script to reproduce sample.
  - For each sampled event include: raw export, transformed SIEM event, original signed blob, and related traces (request_id -> span traces if available).

E. Human-readable artifacts
  - Control mapping appendix mapping event_types to SOC2 trust service criteria and ISO27001 control IDs.
  - Short narrative describing the enforcement flow for RBACv2 (policy change -> validation -> rollout -> enforcement -> log emission).
  - A short chain-of-custody statement for how the bundle was produced and who signed off.

2) Example control mapping (excerpt)
  - event_type: policy.update -> SOC2: CC6.1 (Change Management), ISO27001: A.12.1.2 (Change Control)
  - event_type: authz.decision -> SOC2: CC7.1 (Logical access), ISO27001: A.9.4.1 (Information access restriction)
  - event_type: session.start / session.end -> SOC2: CC6.2 (System operations), ISO27001: A.12.4.1 (Event logging)
  - event_type: admin.login.failed -> SOC2: CC7.2 (Authentication/Unauthorized access), ISO27001: A.9.2.3 (Management of privileged access)

3) SIEM query recipes for auditors (plain-text, non-prod safe examples)
  - Show policy changes in last 30 days: index=rbac-events event_type=policy.update | stats count by change_author, policy_version | sort -count
  - Proof of enforcement (failed decision followed by allow): index=authz event_type=authz.decision outcome=failure | join request_id [search index=authz event_type=authz.decision outcome=success request_id= * ] | table timestamp_utc, actor_id, action, outcome
  - Tamper-evidence bloom: index=evidence-store | stats count by change_diff_hash | where count>1 -> should be 1 (duplicates indicate unexpected replays)

4) Auditor scripts / Q&A talking points (short, rehearsed answers)
  - Q: How do you prove a policy change was authorized and rolled out?
    A: We attach metadata to policy.update events including change_author, change_request_id, and change_diff_hash. The evidence bundle includes the policy PR/Git SHA link (if applicable), CI pipeline run id, and signed artifact in evidence-store. We can replay the change_diff_hash and show the policy prior/after snapshot.

  - Q: How do you ensure logs weren't modified after the fact?
    A: Each raw export is signed and its SHA256 written to an immutable evidence-store backed by object locks. The SIEM transform pipeline includes the original event_id so we can prove the SIEM record correlates to the signed original; the auditor can validate SHA against the stored blob.

  - Q: What are your sampling guarantees?
    A: We use a deterministic seeded sampler (seed value included in the bundle) so the auditor can reproduce the sample from the same time window. Sampling is stratified across event_type and priority to avoid bias.

  - Q: What evidence is available for privileged user activity?
    A: RBACv2 emits admin.login, admin.policy.change, admin.impersonation, and elevated-action events. For each we include session traces, the actor's role history, and whether the action used a privileged token. These are cross-referenced with our access-control change log.

5) Known gaps (current at time of playtest) and remediation plan
  - Gap 1: Missing actor_email in ~0.7% of legacy service events for pre-IdP services.
    Mitigation: annotate events with actor_id mapping table, scheduled migration to include actor_email at ingestion stage by 2024-08-15. Temporary acceptance: we include mapping lookup in the auditor bundle.
  - Gap 2: SIEM transform occasionally drops k8s_pod_hash for queued events during retry floods.
    Mitigation: increase transform worker pool and add retry audit header; long-term fix in pipeline v2 (Q3 release).
  - Gap 3: Evidence bundle generation time currently up to 60m for large windows (not meeting auditor expectation for rapid response).
    Mitigation: optimize bundle generator to parallelize hash verification, target < 15m by 2024-09-01.

6) Playtest checklist (run by sec-compliance + SRE before inviting auditors)
  - Smoke test: generate controlled policy.update and authz.decision flows using test harness; verify event flows to SIEM and presence in evidence-store.
  - Reproducibility: run deterministic sampler using seed in commit and ensure same N events produced.
  - Hash verification: validate SHA256 of raw blobs match values surfaced in bundle.
  - Access audit: request and approve a read-only access token to evidence-store and validate access log is recorded.
  - Bundle sanity: ensure control mapping appendix and chain-of-custody statement included.

7) How auditors will receive the bundle (standard deliverable)
  - A .tar.gz artifact produced by evidence-orch with: /raw_blobs/, /siem_transformed/, /policy_snapshots/, /sample_manifest.json, /repro_scripts/, /control_mapping.md, /access_logs.csv, /signatures.sig.
  - For external auditors we provide a temporary time-limited object-store link and a signed manifest. Internal reviewers can use direct S3 console access with MFA.

8) Repro scripts (what we include)
  - reproduce_sample.sh: given seed, start_time, end_time -> outputs list of event_ids and links to blobs.
  - verify_hashes.py: hashes each raw blob and compares to manifest.
  - siem_table_extract.sql: lightweight exporter used to produce CSV slices for auditor review (no elevated credentials in bundle; uses read-only SIEM export token).

9) Misc notes for the engagement owner (short)
  - Bring the RBAC engineer to the kickoff for policy-change walkthroughs.
  - Expect auditors to ask for a small set of live queries; prepare a secured notebook with pre-authorized read-only tokens.
  - If asked for 3rd party logs (IdP/OAuth provider), be ready to provide signed exports or a support contact with export proof.

Appendix A: quick mapping table (human friendly)
  - Policy lifecycle (create -> review -> approve -> merge -> rollout) maps to: change.request, change.approval, policy.update, policy.roster.apply, policy.enforcement.event.
  - Log retention policy excerpt: auth + admin + rbac-delta -> 365d default; evidence-store signed blobs -> 3y immutability (object-lock).

Appendix B: minimal reproduction example (shell)
  - # Generate a controlled policy update and verify round trip
  - export TEST_PAYLOAD='{"policy": "allow user:read"}'
  curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -d "$TEST_PAYLOAD" https://api.redwood.local/internal/rbacv2/policy | jq .event_id
  # Wait for export to SIEM, then run reproduce script with the returned event_id

Last updated notes: this doc was authored to support the 2024 Q3 SOC 2 readiness playtest. Use the linked Confluence page for canonical control numbering and the Jira ticket list for remediation ownership.

End of document.
